title: ops-product-reliability-lattice-project-plan
content:
Purpose:
This document captures a working plan for the next 8–12 weeks to align product teams and operations on uniform SLOs, handoff patterns, and a small-scale rollout (the "lattice" metaphor = interconnected SLO adapters across services). Goal is to produce: 1) an agreed SLO template for model-serving routes, 2) runbook contracts for handoff to Ops, and 3) a pilot across 3 services with observability hooks and an error budget escalation path.

Context / Why now:
- Product teams are shipping independent model-serving endpoints with different SLAs and no consistent error-budget playbook.
- Platform wants to centralize SLO signals (latency, availability, quality) to enable cross-service fallback and predictable capacity.
- Recent incidents exposed unclear ownership when degradations are service-to-service.

Primary objectives (measurable):
- Consensus SLO template published and checked into repo (slo-configs) by end of week 4.
- Pilot services instrumented with unified telemetry (tracing + tokenized cost + quality signal) and on-call playbooks by week 8.
- Demonstrate automated fallback (higher-latency cheaper model) for 2 services under load spike in staging and record metrics.

Scope (in):
- Production inference routes (hosted + dedicated pools) serving customer-facing APIs; focused on text generation and embeddings first.
- SLO metrics: request success rate, p50/p95/p99 generation latency, model-quality regression signal (from eval harness), and cost-per-token telemetry for routing decisions.

Scope (out):
- Deep model training lifecycle, long-term capacity procurement, non-inference infra (databases, auth) except where cross-service interactions directly affect SLOs.

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Product (hosted-api): Leah Martinez — product owner, SLO acceptance criteria for feature surface.
- Platform Engineering: Maya Chen — project lead, SLO templates, rollout coordination.
- Serving Runtime: Arjun Patel — ensures runtime exposes necessary telemetry and fallback hooks.
- SRE / Ops: Jonah Rivera — runbooks, on-call escalation, incident response.
- Applied ML / Eval: Priya Nair — quality signal design and regression detection.
- Solutions Eng: (TBD) — customer impact mapping for enterprise customers.

Deliverables and acceptance criteria:
1) SLO Template PR in slo-configs: includes metric names, measurement window, alert thresholds, and runbook links. Acceptance: PR merged + feature teams can apply template to a route and get CI lint pass.
2) Runbook contract doc: minimal checklists for handoff (what telemetry, dashboards, alerting, playbook steps). Acceptance: Ops signs off for pilot services.
3) Pilot Implementation: three services (one hosted-api webroute, one dedicated capacity route, one private deployment route) instrumented and demoed. Acceptance: end-to-end test showing fallback during induced spike, with error budget logging.
4) Incident-to-SLO feedback loop: retro template and example, committed to retrospective cadence. Acceptance: run at least one tabletop simulation and record action items.

High-level timeline (8 weeks, sprint-aligned):
- Week 0 (kickoff): Align stakeholders, draft SLO template, identify pilot services. Owner: Maya.
- Week 1–2 (discovery + quick instrumentation): Confirm metric names, map current dashboards, add missing telemetry. Owners: Arjun + Priya.
- Week 3–4 (template & runbook): Iterate SLO PR + runbook checklist, engineering review, Ops sign-off. Owners: Maya + Jonah.
- Week 5–6 (pilot rollout): Apply template to pilot services, wire routing fallback, add alerts and dashboards. Owners: service leads + Platform.
- Week 7 (tabletop & chaos test): Simulate degraded model quality and capacity spike in staging, exercise playbooks. Owners: SRE + Product.
- Week 8 (retrospective + polish): Capture lessons, finalize docs, plan next batch. Owner: Maya.

Communication and rituals:
- Weekly cross-functional sync (30m): status, blockers, decisions — calendar invite: #reliability-lattice-sync.
- SLO design review (bi-weekly): review proposed thresholds and tradeoffs with product and eval.
- On-call shadow week: platform eng will shadow service on-call for pilot services during week 6–7.
- Slack channels: #ops-product-lattice (primary), escalate to #sre-critical for incidents.

Telemetry and signal definition (working list):
- availability.success_rate: success >=200s? define per-service success code set. Measurement window: rolling 30d, alert at 99.95% over 7d (tunable).
- latency.generate_p99_ms: p99 generation latency, window 7d, alert at configurable thresholds per route.
- cost.token_usd: per-request and per-token cost metric to feed routing decisions.
- quality.eval_regression: synthetic eval suite score delta (daily), triggers SLO advisory if model quality drops >2% absolute across critical prompt set.

Error budget policy (proposal):
- Tiered error budget buckets:
  - Tier 1 (core product routes): 0.05% error budget (tight).
  - Tier 2 (aux routes, experiments): 0.5% error budget.
- Automated responses when budget burn rate exceeds threshold: 1) paged advisory to product + SRE, 2) automatic routing to fallback model if configured, 3) circuit-break trigger to reject low-value requests.

Handoff checklist (minimum):
- [ ] Metrics instrumented and visible in dashboard (link).
- [ ] Alerts configured and tested (pager).
- [ ] Runbook created and linked from service README.
- [ ] Owner for each alert defined (primary + secondary).
- [ ] Fallback policy defined (model variant ID, cost delta, expected latency delta).
- [ ] Quality regression prompt set added to eval harness.

Dependencies and blockers:
- Telemetry ingestion capacity: Observability team needs an intake quota for extra traces. (Action: Jonah to open request with observability by 2026-01-22).
- Model catalog tagging: runtime needs stable model IDs surfaced to routing layer. (Action: Arjun to add model-id header in 2 weeks).
- Customer-facing SLA contracts for enterprise customers may constrain automatic fallback. Need Solutions Eng review.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Different product teams disagree on what counts as a "success" for complex responses. Mitigation: default to HTTP-level success + a per-route quality advisory signal; surface disputed cases as advisory channel.
- Risk: Observability cost spike. Mitigation: sample traces for high QPS routes; use aggregated histograms for p95/p99.
- Risk: Fallback harms user experience. Mitigation: limit fallback to non-critical traffic and surface clear telemetry to product teams.

Open questions (to resolve in design review):
- How do we combine model-quality eval signals with latency-based SLOs for a single routing decision (policy precedence)?
- Do we centralize SLO storage in platform repo or leave in each service with linting?
- Thresholds: conservative defaults or product-specific tuning?

Immediate next actions (first two weeks):
- Maya: schedule kickoff and invite stakeholders (done).
- Arjun: produce telemetry mapping doc for the three pilot services by 2026-01-22.
- Priya: draft eval prompt set (initial 100 prompts) by 2026-01-25.
- Jonah: open observability quota request and list required dashboards by 2026-01-24.
- Leah: confirm pilot feature owners and any enterprise customers impacted by fallback by 2026-01-20.

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep the SLO template intentionally minimal — too many metrics = lower adoption.
- Prioritize routes where fallback is straightforward (e.g., classification to smaller model) rather than complex multi-turn chat flows.
- We should try a cheap synthetic traffic generator to validate fallback metrics in staging (use existing chaos infra).

Appendix (examples):
- Example SLO snippet (YAML style — to be converted into PR):
  name: inference.route.latency
  objective: p99 < 1200ms
  window: 7d
  alert: >0.002 (burn rate rule)

- Example runbook headline:
  On-call response: If error budget burn rate > 2x for 3 consecutive 15m windows, page product lead + SRE. If fallback configured, flip routing. Otherwise run mitigation script: revert recent deploys or scale pool as defined.

If you are reading this and want to volunteer a pilot service: ping me (Maya) or add to the spreadsheet linked in the kickoff invite.

Revision history:
- 2026-01-15: initial draft (Maya)
- 2026-01-20: added pilot services list and owners (Leah)
- 2026-01-24: telemetry dependency notes (Jonah)
- 2026-02-10: updated error budget policy proposal (team discussion)
- 2026-03-02: tabletop test scheduled and minor edits (Maya)

Unresolved: need explicit Solutions Eng sign-off process for enterprise SLA exceptions — add as agenda for next sync.
